title: Generic utility library
objective: Practice function templates and concepts in a reproducible, testable C++ implementation.
target_skills: compiler diagnostics and manual code review
prompt: Generic utility library: Function templates and concepts. Implement the exercise in C++20 and document its input contract, expected output, and boundary/failure cases. Compile locally with warnings enabled and test ordinary, boundary and invalid inputs where applicable. The current platform checker performs only a static token smoke-check; it is not a C++ compiler or proof of behavioral correctness, so keep this draft unpublished until isolated execution or human review is in place.
expected_output: A C++ source file implementing generic utility library, plus documented normal, boundary and failure test cases.
acceptance_criteria: Implement the stated behavior and write down valid inputs and expected results.
Compile in explicit C++20 mode with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic and address relevant warnings.
Test an ordinary case, a boundary case, and an invalid/failure case where applicable.
Explain time/space complexity, ownership or portability concerns that apply to the exercise.
Have the implementation behavior reviewed; required-string checks alone are not correctness proof.
hints: Write a brief contract for inputs, outputs and failure cases before coding.
Build a minimal version first, then add validation and meaningful error behavior.
Test boundary cases and review compiler diagnostics; do not mistake token presence for a passing behavioral test.
grading_method: Static required-token smoke check plus human review. There is no production C++ execution runner in this patch; keep the exercise draft until a separate isolated runner or reviewed grading workflow is available.
retry_policy: Retries are permitted. XP is controlled by the existing CodeLeaf backend policy and is granted only for a published exercise whose configured grader succeeds; this draft smoke-check is not ready for publication.
status_note: Draft; reference code is repository-only. Existing contains_all grading only checks tokens and is not behavioral proof; do not publish without isolated execution or human review.
reference_sample_result: The concept documents the operation required by the template. Preconditions should also require low <= high; add a policy for invalid bounds.
